campaigns.context: Over 400 Binance typosquat domains and typedream.app subpages spoof Ledger, Trezor, and Bybit via wallet-setup paths. Random-label bin* domains such as binancee2.com and biiusd.com form the bulk of the infrastructure alongside PaaS-hosted lure pages. Reporters phishunt_io and skocherhan flagged 403 IOCs between 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19.
campaigns.name: Crypto phishing targeting Binance, Ledger, Trezor and Bybit

campaigns.context: Multiple fake Zoom and Google Meet domains deliver RMM payloads via shared kit paths including /Windows/invite.php, /images/ZoomInstaller.msi, and /zoom/Windows across 80-plus domains. Cloudflare Pages subdomains and operator-registered meeting-themed domains both host lures; payloads include TraceRMM, Agta Backup RMM, and Faronics Deploy. Interview and meeting domain names suggest targeting of job seekers.
campaigns.name: Fake Zoom installer phishing via typosquat domains

campaigns.context: Four domain families distribute Android malware impersonating Japanese e-commerce platforms - raku-point-[random].com, rakupoint-[random].com, ruceive-*anpointapp.com, and pontih*-rakunde.com. The ruceive* family splits between Rakuten and Amazon lures; the other families impersonate Rakuten. A single reporter submitted all samples to VirusTotal, covering 68 IOCs from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-12.
campaigns.name: Rakuten/Amazon Android malware on *point* lookalike domains

campaigns.context: Random three-letter paired subdomains under mybluehost.me abuse compromised hosting accounts to distribute Google-branded phishing lures at scale. The uniform two-to-three-level structure (e.g. alz.rgg.mybluehost.me) suggests automated provisioning by a single operator. One reporter flagged 60 IOCs on 2026-08-17.
campaigns.name: Google phishing on compromised subdomains at mybluehost.me

campaigns.context: ValleyRAT C2 infrastructure attributed via local enrichment, covering IPs, MD5 hashes, and SHA256 hashes with no registered domains. C2 IPs include 121.127.253.206 and 202.146.222.95; sideloading DLLs such as nW_Elf.dll appear among the shared hashes. Grouping is based on malware family attribution rather than shared domain or URL patterns. Three reporters flagged 55 indicators from 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-07.
campaigns.name: ValleyRAT C2 infrastructure - IPs and hashes

campaigns.context: Open-directory servers on duckdns.org, ddns.net, and ydns.eu host Remcos, Xworm, and QuasarRAT payloads alongside a crypto trading lure site dexscreenertrade.com, suggesting social-engineering via a fake trading platform. Browsable directories expose staged files across DDNS domains on port 62699. One reporter flagged 54 IOCs between 2026-08-15 and 2026-09-03.
campaigns.name: Remcos and Xworm open-directory staging on DDNS providers

campaigns.context: ClickFix lures on domains including claude-macos-app.com, cli-guides.com, and codex-notes.com redirect malvertising victims to infostealer payloads delivered via /curl/ paths. Domains mimic software brands - Claude AI, Homebrew, and CLI tools - alongside generic business names. Three researchers reported 50 IOCs between 2026-08-13 and 2026-09-10.
campaigns.name: ClickFix malvertising with infostealer via /curl/ paths

campaigns.context: DcRat, AsyncRAT, and XWorm C2 infrastructure spans bitmoon-themed domains (app-bitmoon.fun, trade-bitmoon.fun, verify-bitmoon.fun), a gleeze.com subdomain, DuckDNS nodes, and a GitHub repository. The bitmoon cluster suggests a fake crypto platform used as a social-engineering lure. Enrichment attributes DcRat, AsyncRAT, and Xworm samples to this infrastructure across 47 IOCs as of 2026-09-09.
campaigns.name: DcRat and AsyncRAT C2 on bitmoon-themed and DDNS domains

campaigns.context: Phishing emails use fake cloud-file deletion, storage-suspension, and payment-renewal warnings to pressure victims into immediate payment, routing them to random-name landing domains including financialmarkets.info, budgetweddingplanner.info, schoolgirstrikers.info, and nimblemevia.com. All lures follow the same template and were flagged by a single reporter between 2026-08-25 and 2026-09-11.
campaigns.name: Fake cloud deletion and payment phishing on random domains

campaigns.context: Dozens of subdomains on posmasters.lk, a compromised domain, host Google-branded phishing pages with labels ranging from business names to project identifiers, suggesting automated provisioning on a hijacked site. The pattern mirrors a concurrent campaign abusing mybluehost.me for the same Google lure type. One reporter flagged 38 IOCs on 2026-08-17.
campaigns.name: Google phishing on compromised subdomains at posmasters.lk

campaigns.context: Attackers impersonate TrustWallet and MetaMask to steal seed phrases via fraudulent airdrop and wallet-restore lures. Two domain families form the infrastructure: trust-prefixed .com domains (trustwallet*, trustyourcrypt*, trust-wazirx.com) and wallet-account* .com domains with trust.* subdomains. skocherhan flagged both clusters on 2026-08-15.
campaigns.name: TrustWallet and crypto wallet seed-phrase phishing

campaigns.name: Apple and Roblox login-page phishing on random-label domains

campaigns.context: Domains embedding restore in their names impersonate TrustWallet and MetaMask wallets for seed-phrase theft via fake airdrop lures - restoremywallets.com, restoretrustwallet.com, restorebasetrust.com - alongside a Google credential harvester at restoration-google.com. campaigns.name: MioLab macOS stealer via fake Adobe InDesign DMG installer

campaigns.name: Cloaking gambling funnel via sqllq.com

campaigns.name: Scotiabank, Rogers, and hotel-themed phishing on hezhiad.com

campaigns.name: Prime Video phishing lure staged on AWS S3 bucket
